Compilation of Real-World LLM & AI Agent Use Cases in Financial Services

### Context Large language models (LLMs) and AI agents are transforming financial services: from streamlining regulatory compliance and accelerating deal analysis to personalizing customer experiences and automating complex workflows across banking, trading, and asset management. This repository curates real-world LLM and agentic AI implementations in finance, showcasing enterprise platforms, specialized models, and integrated solutions deployed by leading financial institutions worldwide. Have a great example of LLMs in the financial services sector? Contribute by opening a **pull request** or submitting an **issue**. [![Contributions Welcome!](https://img.shields.io/badge/Contributions-Welcome-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](./CONTRIBUTING.md) ___ ### 📑 Table of Contents - [Retail & Commercial Banking](#banking) - Covers personal and business banking services—checking and savings accounts, mortgages, SME financing, and credit solutions. Also addresses central banking operations, digital transformation in traditional banks, and AI-driven advisory for both retail and corporate clients. - [Wealth & Asset Management](#wealth) - Encompasses asset and wealth advisory, mutual funds, private equity, institutional asset management, robo-advisory, and portfolio management for high-net-worth individuals and institutional clients. - [Capital Markets & Trading](#markets) - Covers investment banking, securities trading, market infrastructure, equity research, credit analysis, and financial market analytics. Includes broker-dealers, exchanges, and financial data platforms. - [Payments & Transaction Services](#payments) - Focuses on digital payments, card networks, cross-border transactions, BNPL, and payment infrastructure. Also highlights AI-based fraud detection, risk assessment, and automated payment processing innovations. - [Insurance & Risk Management](#insurance) - Addresses life, health, property, and casualty insurance, along with reinsurance, underwriting automation, and actuarial modeling. Features AI-driven claims processing, fraud detection, personalized policy recommendations, and broader risk assessment tools. Each example can be classified into one of 3 categories based on type of use case: - **Enterprise Platform**: Large-scale LLM deployments spanning multiple lines of business or the entire organization. These implementations typically address a broad range of tasks—such as customer support, internal operations, and compliance—within a unified, centrally managed framework. - **Fine-Tuned Model**: Models either pre-trained or fine-tuned on focused datasets (e.g., regulatory filings, financial news) to achieve deep domain expertise. By narrowing the training data to specific tasks and terminology, they deliver higher accuracy and more relevant insights than general-purpose models. - **Integrated Solution**: Vendor-provided or off-the-shelf AI solutions deployed for specific workflows and use cases. Financial institutions leverage ready-made integrations, cloud services, and prompt engineering to streamline tasks—such as AI-powered chatbots or document processing—without extensive internal development. ___ ## Retail & Commercial Banking | Name | Type | Date | Description | Site | Paper | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | HSBCnio | Integrated Solution | Oct 2026 | HSBC launched HSBCnio, an AI-enabled corporate and institutional transaction banking platform that exposes authorized account and transaction data via HSBC's Model Context Protocol (MCP). Corporate treasury teams connect internal AI tools on a read-only basis — under existing HSBCnet logins and permissions — for liquidity forecasting, variance analysis, cross-border cash balance analysis, and reporting, alongside APIs and a planned "Ask HSBC" query feature. Rolled out in Hong Kong (~4,000 multinational regional offices); no external LLM vendor is named. | [🔗](https://www.about.hsbc.com.hk/news-and-media/hsbc-launches-new-ai-enabled-solution-to-transform-transaction-banking) | - | | NatWest Complaint Investigation Agent | Integrated Solution | Oct 2026 | NatWest AI Research deployed a single-agent complaint investigation system built on the OpenAI Agents SDK, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1-nano into UK retail banking production (distinct from Cora). The agent queries 16 read-only, Pydantic-validated tools across call transcripts, KYC, and dispute records to assemble source-cited chronological timelines and policy-aligned summaries for human handler review under FCA rules. Across 1,234 production complaints (~120k median tokens), it matched or exceeded human investigations in 90% of 187 expert-paired cases, cutting median time from 30 minutes to 23 seconds. | - | [🔗](https://aclanthology.org/2026.emnlp-industry.227/) | | PRAGMA (Revolut) | Fine-Tuned Model | Oct 2026 | Revolut pre-trained PRAGMA, a family of encoder-only Transformer foundation models (10M, 100M, and 1B parameters), on 24 billion banking events (207 billion tokens) from 26 million pseudonymised user records across 111 countries, outperforming task-specific baselines on credit scoring, external fraud, product recommendation, and LTV prediction while eliminating weeks of manual feature engineering. # Contribution Guide

This repository tracks real-world LLM implementations in financial services. Contributions are welcome via pull request or issue.

## Submission Guidelines

1. Verify your contribution isn't already listed (updates to existing entries are welcome)
2. Use reputable sources, ideally not behind paywalls
3. Choose the appropriate section:
   - Retail & Commercial Banking
   - Wealth Management & Capital Markets
   - Payments & FinTech
   - Insurance & Risk Management

## Entry Format

```
| Company/Model Name | Type | Month Year | Brief description | [🔗](https://source_link.com) | [🔗](https://paper_link.com) |
```

Implementation types:
- Enterprise Platform - Organization-wide deployments across multiple business lines
- Integrated Solution - Vendor solutions or cloud services for specific workflows
- Fine-Tuned Model - Domain-specific models trained on financial data

Writing descriptions (1-2 sentences, ~50-70 words):
- Include: company name, technology/LLM used, specific use cases, quantifiable impact
- Focus on measurable results and scale indicators
- Example: "BNY developed Eliza, an enterprise AI platform powered by OpenAI models, enabling 20,000 employees to build AI agents across 125+ live use cases. The platform reduces legal contract review time by 75% for 3,000+ annual vendor agreements."

Review existing README entries for reference, or open an issue for questions.

Thank you for contributing!
